7hz-aurora: Detailed, airy and tight-bassed with a wide stage; the highs turn sharp at higher volumes.
7hz-five: Heavy, fun bass that stays defined, in a compact shell; mids sit back and highs can run hot.
aful-explorer: Warm, lush and relaxing with punchy bass and a secure fit; the dark treble lacks detail for some.
apple-airpods-4-with-active-noise-cancel: Very comfortable open-style earbud with convenient use; noise cancelling helps but is not perfect.
apple-airpods-5: Open-style buds with surprisingly strong noise cancelling and fuller bass than the last open pair.
apple-airpods-max-2: Class-leading noise cancelling and a sturdy metal build; heavy, pricey and tiring after a few hours.
apple-airpods-pro-2: Easy everyday earbud with a good mic for calls, though they slip out during workouts.
apple-airpods-pro-3: New tips fit securely for many; others feel pressure, and some find music a step back from Pro 2.
audeze-crbn: Lifelike, clear electrostatic sound with real bass weight and a light fit; needs a strong amp, costly.
audeze-lcd-s20: Fast, tight and revealing sound that suits gaming and comfortable wear; a few find the tuning dull.
audio-technica-ath-adx3000: Airy, detailed open sound that is very light and easy to drive; the treble runs bright for several.
audio-technica-ath-adx7000: Wide, lifelike sound with real bass weight, light and comfy; the stiff cable is noisy, needs an amp.
audio-technica-ath-m20x: Very good budget studio pair that is comfy and tough; the bass is thin and the cord is fixed.
audio-technica-ath-r30x: Light, comfy entry open-back with a lively, spacious sound; the fixed cord and small pads draw gripes.
audio-technica-ath-r70x: Uncoloured, open sound with excellent imaging and very light comfort; needs an amp, bass is moderate.
beyerdynamic-amiron-300: Small, comfortable earbuds with strong noise cancelling and a balanced default tune; some had glitches.
beyerdynamic-dt-1770-pro-mkii: Powerful bass, accurate imaging and great comfort; some hear a treble spike, a few find the cups small.
beyerdynamic-dt-1990-pro: Open, exciting and detailed with hard-hitting bass; treble is harsh for many, headbands fail for a few.
beyerdynamic-dt-880-edition: Wide, precise imaging and all-day comfort; the bass is lean, the highs sharp, and it needs a strong amp.
beyerdynamic-dt-990-edition: Punchy bass, a wide stage and very comfortable pads; the highs can turn sharp and tiring.
bose-quietcomfort-headphones: Very comfortable with strong noise cancelling for flights; the bassy tuning and ear pressure bother some.
bose-quietcomfort-headphones-2nd-gen: Plush comfort and strong noise cancelling with warm, bassy sound; plastic feels cheap, bass runs heavy.
bose-quietcomfort-ultra-earbuds: Class-leading noise cancelling with weighty bass; some find it too bassy or pricey, no wireless charging.
bose-quietcomfort-ultra-earbuds-2nd-gen: Noise cancelling that most owners rate as the best they have used; a few had ear pain.
bose-ultra-open-earbuds: All-day comfort and an open fit that keeps you aware; pricey, with little bass and no isolation.
bowers-wilkins-pi8: Clear, spacious sound owners call their best in earbuds; a few report connection or charging issues.
campfire-audio-alien-brain: Warm, smooth and balanced with tight bass and natural vocals; compact shells fit snugly.
campfire-audio-andromeda-10: Airy, wide and musical with fast, textured bass; the odd shells fit some ears poorly, and it's pricey.
dan-clark-audio-aeon-2-open: Very comfortable, warm and detailed with natural staging; some find the bass boomy, and it wants an amp.
dunu-alpha-3: Wide, smooth mids and vocals with a solid metal build for the price; bass is light on some fits.
dunu-dn242: Vocal-forward sound with plenty of detail and punchy bass; comfortable, with few complaints.
dunu-kima-2: Warm-neutral tuning with standout vocals at good value; the small flat shells do not fit everyone.
focal-bathys-mg: Detailed, spacious wireless sound with a praised wired USB mode; noise cancelling is merely good.
grado-gs1000: A favourite for many, with excellent bass, detail and stage; heavy, and the pads press after a few hours.
grado-rs1: Open, lively and detailed with punchy bass; the pads and fit are uncomfortable, and it feels cheap.
grado-sr60: Lively, open sound that suits rock and metal and is great value; on-ear pads can hurt after hours.
grado-sr80: Fun, lively sound for rock and metal at a fair price; the cable, build and fit draw some complaints.
hifiman-arya-organic: Big soundstage and resolution at a fair price, but the bright treble fatigues some and many use EQ.
hifiman-arya-stealth: Huge soundstage and imaging; the recurring gripe is quality control, with several failing drivers.
hifiman-audivina: Huge, airy stage and high detail for a closed-back; a few report tuning faults and poor isolation.
hifiman-edition-xs: Outstanding value with a wide, open soundstage; the main complaint is build and quality control.
hifiman-he600: Clear, detailed planar sound with crisp highs and comfy wear; it needs a good amp and can sound bright.
hifiman-sundara: Detailed, balanced step up from cheaper headphones; many report dead or buzzing drivers.
hifiman-susvara-unveiled: Spacious, very detailed sound that is easier to power than before and comfy; exposed drivers are fragile.
juzear-defiant: Detailed sound that owners love for the price; the shell is a fit gamble and needs the right tips.
kiwi-ears-ardor: Huge battery, effective noise cancelling and punchy bass, and fits over glasses; sharp highs and no app.
kiwi-ears-astral: Clean, detailed sound and sharp imaging for competitive gaming; the large shell hurts some ears.
kiwi-ears-atheia: Luxurious wood build and comfort with a roomy stage; the bass runs boomy and the tuning feels unfinished.
kiwi-ears-aventus: Comfortable, good value and long battery life with fun bass; plastic hinges squeak for a few.
kiwi-ears-canta: Natural vocals and tight bass in small, comfy shells; treble gets bright at higher volume for several.
kiwi-ears-division: Heavy, punchy bass in a light, comfy build with two cables; bass can drown vocals and hinges feel weak.
kiwi-ears-ellipse: Balanced, slightly warm sound with punchy bass in a light, plush fit; the stage is modest and it leaks.
kiwi-ears-halcyon: Strong, deep bass in light, comfortable metal shells; some find the tuning too polite and safe.
kiwi-ears-stardust: Smooth, relaxed highs and comfortable small shells; many hear boxy or nasal vocals and light bass.
kz-as24-pro: Detailed, punchy and warm for the price, with forward vocals and useful switches; some find it surgical.
kz-axas: Clear footsteps and plug-and-play USB-C for gaming in a light fit; bass is thin, a few had imbalance.
kz-carol: Very cheap wireless buds with punchy, bassy sound and useful noise cancelling; a few hear thin sound.
kz-carol-pro: Great-value wireless buds with warm, bassy sound and LDAC; the case rattles and bass can feel polite.
kz-duet: Punchy, fun bass and a comfortable semi-open fit that suits gaming; the cable is fixed and the mic tugs.
kz-duonic: Very low cost with crisp, detailed sound; many say the bass is lighter than the marketing suggests.
kz-krila: Very cheap with detail and punchy bass that beat its price; the highs can be sharp and mids thin.
kz-pisces: Airy, detailed highs and easy driving for a low price; treble-sensitive listeners find it sharp.
kz-prx: Surprisingly good cheap way into planar sound; it benefits from a decent DAC and is hard to drive.
letshuoer-astralis: Warm, fun planar with strong bass and smooth treble; a few find it less technical than rivals.
letshuoer-dx1: Natural, rich vocals and smooth treble you can play loud; the bass is polite and the highs soft.
letshuoer-s12-pro: Clear, energetic sound that improves with EQ, though the short, angled nozzle is hard to seal.
letshuoer-s12-ultra: Fast planar bass and smooth treble in a small, comfortable shell; soundstage is not its strength.
letshuoer-s15: Smooth, warm planar with good detail and a spacious stage; a few say it is hard to justify at full price.
meze-105-silva: Plush, comfortable and beautifully built with smooth, natural mids; bass is lean, highs can get bright.
meze-109-pro: Warm, punchy and comfortable, said to suit rock and metal; some find the treble a touch sharp.
meze-advar: Silky, natural and full-bodied sound in tiny shells you can lie down in; hard-to-find nozzle filters.
meze-alba: Tiny, light and easy to wear for hours, though some find the sound thin or bass-light.
meze-elite-tungsten: Spacious, detailed and very comfortable with a wide stage and excellent control; one owner was let down.
meze-poet: Gorgeous build, very comfortable and warm, easy to drive; highs can be sharp and the frame creaks.
moondrop-horizon: Very light, warm and easy on the ears; many find the sound dark with soft bass and a loose headband.
moondrop-illustrious: Compact, comfortable metal shells with a warm, relaxed sound; light bass and doubts about its price.
moondrop-old-fashioned: Very cheap, light open-back on-ear with an open sound; the bass is thin, which many fix with EQ.
moondrop-quark-2: Very cheap with a built-in DAC and a comfortable shell; bass is light and the fit is poor for some.
moondrop-quarks: Very cheap, warm and fun for a tiny driver; reviewers report microphonics and cables that fail.
moondrop-rays: Comfortable low-profile fit and a smooth, warm, balanced sound; finish and plug wear for a few.
moondrop-space-travel: Pleasant sound and decent noise cancelling for very little money; the mic and features are basic.
moondrop-space-travel-2: Likeable sound at low cost, with a few buying a second pair; some report fit or battery problems.
moondrop-starfield-iii: Natural, clean sound with lovely female vocals and a USB-C EQ plug; the bass is light and the highs safe.
moondrop-ultrasonic: Clean, textured tuning with low lag and a wide stage; noise cancelling is modest and LDAC drains battery.
oneplus-buds-4: Strong noise cancelling and transparency for the price; bass runs heavy and a few report battery trouble.
philips-shp9500: Comfortable and a cheap open-back that many love for gaming; some find the mids foggy and bass light.
sennheiser-accentum-plus-wireless: Long 50-hour battery and a comfortable fit with good adaptive noise cancelling; sound is only competent.
sennheiser-accentum-true-wireless: Comfortable, pocketable buds with strong noise cancelling; volume runs quiet and the battery is short.
sennheiser-accentum-wireless: Long battery life and a comfortable, easygoing fit; some report lag, cheap feel or playback glitches.
sennheiser-hd-25: Controlled, punchy bass, tiny size and excellent isolation; the strong clamp makes ears sore after hours.
sennheiser-hd-280-pro: Detailed, well isolating and good value for tracking; the clamp is tight and the build can fail.
sennheiser-hd-300-pro: Comfortable, well isolating and detailed for monitoring, with less clamp than older closed models.
sennheiser-hd-400-pro: Clear, detailed and light with low sibilance, well liked for mixing; some find it plasticky or clampy.
sennheiser-hd-400s: Cheap, comfortable and balanced for years of use; reviewers split on bass, and a few found it flimsy.
sennheiser-hd-505: Light, comfy and airy with natural vocals and a wide stage; the bass is light and they leak sound.
sennheiser-hd-569: Plush comfort for hours of listening and good value; some find it cramped, shouty or a bit flat.
sennheiser-hd-600: Natural, smooth mids that many keep returning to for years; the strong clamp bothers a good number.
sennheiser-hd-650: Warm, smooth midrange kept by many for years; a few find it dull or veiled and want a decent amp.
sennheiser-hd-800-s: Expansive soundstage and imaging with long-session comfort; the common complaint is thin bass.
sennheiser-hd-820: Huge stage and pinpoint imaging for a closed-back with a comfortable fit; pricey and bass can get messy.
sennheiser-ie-100-pro: Light, secure and clear with good isolation for stage and travel; the proprietary cable limits swaps.
sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless: Huge battery with a replaceable cell, rich bass and all-day comfort; noise cancelling trails rivals.
sennheiser-momentum-true-wireless-5: Sound and noise cancelling that several prefer to the AirPods Pro 3.
simgot-ea1000-fermat: Detailed, clean sound with swappable tuning nozzles and a luxe build; the highs get sharp for many.
simgot-ea2000: Bright, detailed sound with a wide stage and strong bass for some; treble gets hot and tiring.
simgot-eg280: Crisp detail and sharp imaging for gaming at a low price with a comfy shell; highs can tire.
simgot-em10: Deep, textured bass with a smooth, clean sound and a comfortable fit; mids sit back and can get hazy.
simgot-ep5: Light, comfortable and warm with punchy bass for the price; the pads get hot and the cable rubs noisily.
simgot-et142: Detailed, punchy and well built with comfy stock tips and cable; the vocal and treble push isn't for all.
simgot-ew300: Detailed, comfortable all-rounder with swappable nozzles at a low price; some find the treble sharp.
simgot-supermix-5: Rich, unified sound with tactile bone-conduction bass and smooth highs; the bass is not very heavy.
sony-ier-m9: Warm, non-fatiguing sound with top imaging in light, comfy shells; a bit polite, and it wants a good amp.
sony-linkbuds-clip: Very comfortable open buds with good battery life; expensive, weak on bass, and calls draw criticism.
sony-linkbuds-fit: Light, stable fit that stays put in workouts, with forceful bass; isolation and cancelling are modest.
sony-linkbuds-open: Comfortable open-ear buds with surprisingly meaty mids and bass; weak in noise and fit varies.
sony-linkbuds-s: Light, well built and good enough at noise cancelling for daily use; a couple report battery faults.
sony-mdr-cd900st: Clear, vocal-focused studio sound that owners love; the thin stock pads hurt and the cable is fixed.
sony-mdr-z1r: Comfortable, luxurious build and a big stage with strong bass; some hear veiled mids and sharp treble.
sony-ult-wear: Huge, rumbly bass with strong noise cancelling for the price; the bass overwhelms the mids for many.
sony-wf-1000xm6: Noise cancelling many call the best they have tried, with long battery; fit is the snag for some.
sony-wf-c510: Light, comfortable and solid sounding for the price, with long battery; no noise cancelling, soft highs.
sony-wf-c710n: Strong noise cancelling and good value with long battery; the default tune needs EQ, fit slips for a few.
sony-wh-1000xm4: Excellent noise cancelling and comfort that suits EQ; several find it muddy or bassy, and swivels broke.
sony-wh-1000xm6: Excellent noise cancelling, good mics and a travel-friendly fold; stock sound is muddy until you EQ it.
sony-wh-ch520: Light with a very long battery and decent, EQ-friendly sound for the price; small cups hurt many ears.
sony-wh-ch720n: Light, comfortable and long-lasting with punchy bass for the price; cheap plastic, average cancelling.
tanchjim-force: Clear vocals, a wide stage and a handy USB-C EQ plug; the stock bass runs light and it needs tweaking.
tanchjim-nora: Clean, detailed, warm-leaning sound and a comfy fit with good vocals; a few have cable or tip issues.
tanchjim-ola-ii: Warm, lively and good value with a spacious feel; some find the bass soft and boomy.
tanchjim-soda: Smooth, detailed sound with controlled bass and a wide stage; some find it lean and a few get ear pain.
tangzu-nezha: Silky, natural vocals with great comfort and isolation; the bass is polite and lacks real slam.
tangzu-tianpeng: Lifelike vocals and a big, precise stage with great accessories; the bass is tame and the shells huge.
tangzu-waner-s-g: Light, comfortable and vocal-focused with warm, natural sound for cheap; can tire on energetic music.
tangzu-xuannv: Clean, warm bass and smooth, safe highs for long listening; some want more sparkle, and it needs power.
tangzu-xuanwu-gate: Huge stage, strong detail and rich vocals; light bass punch, and big shells and sharp highs bother some.
tangzu-xue-tao: Good detail and a detachable mic for the price, easy to drive; some report a quiet mic or a broken cable.
thieaudio-cypher: Natural, studio-style vocals with deep bass and a sturdy build; the stage is close and clamp firm.
thieaudio-hype-4-mkii: Detailed, sturdy and comfortable with natural vocals for the money; the highs run bright for several.
thieaudio-legacy-2: Neutral, forgiving sound with great comfort and isolation; the bass is lean and the highs gentle.
thieaudio-legacy-4: Fast, detailed and punchy in small comfy shells; the bright treble gets tiring for many.
thieaudio-monarch-mkiv: Clean, detailed sound with a wide stage and strong bass; the large shells cause ear pain for many.
thieaudio-oracle-mkii: Hard-hitting, detailed bass and clear vocals with a lively top end; the treble runs hot for several.
thieaudio-prestige: Owners call it endgame for its clean, airy, accurate sound; a few had fit or build problems.
thieaudio-v16-divinity: Silky, detailed and non-fatiguing with a huge stage; bulky shells suit small ears poorly, bass is polite.
truthear-nova: Detailed and fairly balanced, but opinions are split: some call it shouty, narrow or foam-dependent.
